basis: Neoplasm arising in the paranasal sinuses, which belong to the airway axis; lymphoma is only one subtype.
Reactive cystic inflammation of the bladder; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Pituitary deficiency and polydactyly define syndrome; developmental delay reported in 3/3; cleft palate in 1/3. Isolated urinary findings omitted under cap.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability and digital malformations define syndrome; congenital absence of nails in 7/7 supports dermatologic involvement.
Tumor confined to the placenta, an obstetric organ outside the axes; its fetal vascular origin does not establish maternal cardiovascular disease.
Autonomic bladder dysfunction defines the condition; reflux, hydronephrosis and CKD each reported in 2/5. Slow pupillary response alone does not establish ocular damage.
Anorectal malformation defines syndrome; HPO reports nephropathy 80-99% and hearing impairment 30-79%. Renal annotation conflicts with the definition's stated absence.
Tumor of the chest wall, comprising the skeletal and associated soft tissues; lung involvement is not inherent.
Isolated sperm flagellar abnormalities cause male infertility; reproductive function has no axis and endocrine dysfunction is not described.
Syndromic growth disorder with characteristic skeletal asymmetry and digital abnormalities; hypoglycemia is characteristic. Listed tumors and urinary anomalies are not universal features.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Adenocarcinoma originating in gallbladder epithelium; gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
Primary biliary cholangitis is an autoimmune disease damaging intrahepatic bile ducts.
Developmental disability and structural brain anomalies define disease; scoliosis occurs in 2/5 (40%). Feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Autoimmune injury to the nervous system defines this umbrella; additional organs depend on the specific subtype.
Nutrient deficiency causes metabolic dysfunction; affected downstream organs vary by vitamin and do not apply across most of the umbrella.
Congenital myopathy with lung hypoplasia 2/3; cleft palate 3/3; urinary obstruction/hydronephrosis 1/3 and renal hypoplasia reported. Single-case ocular findings omitted under cap.
Inherited generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures; no other organ damage is established.
Childhood tumor originating in the testis, a reproductive organ; endocrine origin or hormone dysfunction is not established.
Surfactant deficiency and immature lungs cause alveolar collapse and respiratory failure; disseminated coagulation is a complication, not a common defining feature.
Sensory/autonomic neuropathy; chronic intestinal dysmotility is a defining gastrointestinal manifestation. Fractures and wounds are secondary traumatic injuries.
This concept denotes the cataract itself; associated myotonic dystrophy is the underlying disease rather than additional damage caused by the cataract.
Severe neurologic impairment and skin/hair pigment abnormalities define disease; myopia occurs in 30-79%. Optic atrophy and macular dystrophy occur in only 5-29%.
Progressive epileptic encephalopathy with dystonia and developmental regression; respiratory infections are separate infections and feeding difficulty alone is insufficient.
Focal autoimmune stiff-person syndrome causes abnormal motor activity, rigidity and spasms; these do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
